expectations.evidence: 'Vague claims instead of specifics. Bly keeps stressing that specific copy sells and general copy doesn't' and Ultra-specific scored 1: '"Products," "quality" and "great" are all abstract.' (Note: the verdict also calls it a 'blind' headline, which misapplies Bly's term, since a blind headline is one that makes no sense without the body copy, but the vagueness point itself is correct.)

expectations.text: Applies the four functions of a headline (attention, select audience, deliver message, draw into body)
expectations.evidence: Section 1 'The four jobs of a headline' lists and evaluates get attention, select the audience, deliver a complete message, draw the reader into the body copy; matches SKILL.md.
Section 2 scores Urgent 1, Unique 1, Ultra-specific 1, Useful 1 = 4/16, and rescores the recommended rewrite (2/3/4/4 = 13/16).

expectations.text: Gives multiple rewrites using named techniques or types
expectations.evidence: Seven rewrites in a table labeled Direct, How-to, Question, Reason-why, News, Testimonial, Command (all among Bly's 8 types), with a sample furniture-store business, and a recommended rewrite.

expectations.text: Mentions USP or a BFD/motivator angle
expectations.evidence: No mention of a USP, Rosser Reeves, the BFD formula (beliefs, feelings, desires) or the copy motivators anywhere. The closest points are 'Unique' in the 4 U's and 'the single most important benefit', which are not the USP or BFD/motivator frameworks. It also adds unsupported claims ('Bly prefers sentence case').
